revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Middle School Fundraiser
revealWordProblem.text: Some sixth-grade students will make 50 bags of honey granola to sell at a fundraising event using the recipe shown. They will put 2 cups of granola in each bag and will sell each bag for $5. Choose one question to answer. Question 1: How many cups of rolled oats will the students need to buy? Question 2: One pound of almonds costs $9.99 and has 3 cups of almonds. How much will the students need to budget for almonds?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Question 1: The recipe makes 6 cups of granola using 4 cups of rolled oats, so rolled oats to total granola is a 4:6 ratio. The students need 50 bags × 2 cups = 100 cups of granola in all. Scaling the ratio: 100 ÷ 6 × 4 = 66 2/3 cups of rolled oats. They need to buy about 66 2/3 cups of rolled oats.

vocabulary.definition: Use a ratio to compare two quantities by division.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Usar una razón para comparar dos cantidades mediante la división.
vocabulary.visual: 3 red tiles to 5 blue tiles can be written 3:5 or 3/5.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare two amounts, like 3 to 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar dos cantidades, como 3 a 2.
vocabulary.cloze: A comparison of two quantities, like 3 to 5, is a ___.

examples.why: A single number does not compare two quantities.

vocabulary.definition: Looking at two or more amounts to see how they are related.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Mirar dos o más cantidades para ver cómo se relacionan.

vocabulary.cloze: Showing how two amounts relate to each other is a ___.

examples.why: It looks at two amounts to see how they relate.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio comparing one part of a group to another part.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara una parte de un grupo con otra parte.
vocabulary.visual: 3 cups flour : 2 cups sugar (ingredient to ingredient)
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio that compares one part of a group to another part is a ___ ratio.

examples.why: It compares one part to another part.

vocabulary.definition: A bar cut into equal parts that shows how two amounts in a ratio compare, and how they make up the whole.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una barra dividida en partes iguales que muestra cómo se comparan dos cantidades de una razón y cómo forman el total.

examples.text: A bar with parts of different sizes and no labels

vocabulary.definition: Two number lines lined up so matching tick marks show the two quantities in a ratio at the same time.

examples.text: One line showing only cups of drink

launch.narrative: This is your challenge small group for Lesson 3.1. You can already get the answer — so in here the answer is the starting point. We ask when the method holds, when it breaks, and how you would convince someone who disagrees.
noticePrompts: What two ingredients are being compared in the recipe?
How could you describe the relationship between apple juice and sparkling water?
Is the amount of apple juice more than, less than, or equal to the amount of sparkling water?
wonderPrompts: What if we compared the sparkling water to the apple juice instead — would the ratio change?
Could we compare one ingredient to the total amount of both?
launch.contextImage: A kitchen counter with measuring cups showing 3 cups of apple juice and 2 cups of sparkling water beside a recipe card

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — What is a ratio?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: A ratio compares two quantities, and the order you write them in matters. You can write a ratio in words or with a colon, and you can draw it with a tape diagram or a double number line — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Chef Reyes uses 3 cups of apple juice for every 2 cups of sparkling water.
I am comparing two amounts: apple juice and sparkling water.
I write apple juice to sparkling water, in that order, as 3 to 2, or 3:2.
I can also draw the ratio. On a tape diagram I give apple juice 3 equal parts and sparkling water 2 equal parts, so one batch is 5 parts in all.
Those same 5 parts show a second ratio: apple juice to the whole fruit drink is 3 to 5.
On a double number line I line the two amounts up: 5 cups of fruit drink pairs with 3 cups of apple juice, and 10 cups of fruit drink pairs with 6 cups of apple juice.
linesEs: El chef Reyes usa 3 tazas de jugo de manzana por cada 2 tazas de agua mineral.
Estoy comparando dos cantidades: jugo de manzana y agua mineral.
Escribo jugo de manzana a agua mineral, en ese orden, como 3 a 2, o 3:2.
También puedo dibujar la razón. En un diagrama de barras le doy al jugo de manzana 3 partes iguales y al agua mineral 2 partes iguales, así que una tanda son 5 partes en total.
Esas mismas 5 partes muestran una segunda razón: jugo de manzana al total de la bebida es 3 a 5.
En una recta numérica doble alineo las dos cantidades: 5 tazas de bebida se emparejan con 3 tazas de jugo de manzana, y 10 tazas de bebida se emparejan con 6 tazas de jugo de manzana.

weDo.title: Try it together — then prove it
lines: A bowl has 4 apples and 1 orange. What two amounts are we comparing?
We write apples to oranges in order: 4 to 1, or 4:1.
Now draw it: 4 equal parts for apples beside 1 part for oranges, 5 parts of fruit in all.
So apples to total fruit is 4 to 5.
Now prove it: say why that move had to work at all — not just that it did.
Sentence frame — convince a skeptic: "My method works because ___ . It would stop working if ___ ."
linesEs: Un tazón tiene 4 manzanas y 1 naranja. ¿Qué dos cantidades estamos comparando?
Escribimos manzanas a naranjas en orden: 4 a 1, o 4:1.
Ahora dibújalo: 4 partes iguales para las manzanas junto a 1 parte para la naranja, 5 partes de fruta en total.
Entonces manzanas al total de fruta es 4 a 5.
Ahora demuéstralo: di por qué ese paso tenía que funcionar — no solo que funcionó.
Marco de oración — convence a alguien que duda: «Mi método funciona porque ___ . Dejaría de funcionar si ___ .»

youDo.title: Now you try — and defend it
lines: Try the problems below on your own. Getting the answer is half the work — be ready to say why your method works, and where it would stop working.
Then pick one problem and show it a second way. If two different methods agree, that agreement is your proof.
linesEs: Intenta los problemas de abajo por tu cuenta. Obtener la respuesta es la mitad del trabajo — prepárate para decir por qué funciona tu método y dónde dejaría de funcionar.
Luego elige un problema y muéstralo de una segunda manera. Si dos métodos distintos coinciden, esa coincidencia es tu prueba.

conceptIntro.headingEs: Ve más allá — ¿Qué es una razón?
conceptIntro.introEs: Esto ya lo sabes hacer. Así que subimos de nivel, no de número: halla lo que siempre es cierto, muéstralo de una segunda manera y prepárate para defenderlo con una razón en lugar de una respuesta.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Una razón compara dos cantidades, y el orden en que las escribes importa. Puedes escribir una razón con palabras o con dos puntos, y puedes dibujarla con un diagrama de barras o una recta numérica doble — y puedes decir por qué es cierto y dónde dejaría de serlo.

diagram.title: 45 Cups of Fruit Drink for the Whole Grade
diagram.caption: One batch of Chef Reyes's recipe is 3 cups of apple juice and 2 cups of sparkling water, so one batch makes 5 cups of fruit drink. 45 cups takes 9 of those equal batches, which is 9 x 3 = 27 cups of apple juice and 9 x 2 = 18 cups of sparkling water — and 27 + 18 = 45.

diagram.title: Double number line: apple juice and fruit drink
diagram.caption: The ratio 3:5 holds at every tick, so the pairs scale together: triple the drink from 15 to 45 cups and the juice triples from 9 to 27 cups.

onLevel.stem: A fruit salad has 5 pieces of melon, 3 pieces of pineapple, and 2 grapes. What is the ratio of pineapple to melon?
onLevel.explanation: The ratio of pineapple to melon compares pineapple (3) to melon (5), so the ratio is 3:5.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
That compares pineapple to the total (5 + 3 + 2). The question compares pineapple to melon only.
You started with the pineapple, which fits the order — but 2 is the number of grapes. Re-read which two amounts the question compares.
hints: Three fruits are listed, but the question only compares pineapple and melon — the grapes are extra info.
Pick out just the two amounts you need, then write them in the order the question names: pineapple first.
Circle the pineapple count (3) and the melon count (5). Write them in the order 'pineapple to melon.'
onLevel.stemEs: Una ensalada de frutas tiene 5 trozos de melón, 3 trozos de piña y 2 uvas. ¿Cuál es la razón de piña a melón?
onLevel.explanationEs: La razón de piña a melón compara la piña (3) con el melón (5), así que la razón es 3:5.
hintsEs: Se mencionan tres frutas, pero la pregunta solo compara piña y melón — las uvas son información de más.
Escoge solo las dos cantidades que necesitas y escríbelas en el orden que nombra la pregunta: la piña primero.
Encierra la cantidad de piña (3) y la de melón (5). Escríbelas en el orden 'piña a melón'.

onLevel.stem: A parking lot has 10 cars and 6 trucks. What is the part-to-whole ratio of trucks to total vehicles?
onLevel.explanation: Total vehicles = 10 + 6 = 16. The ratio of trucks to total is 6:16.
choiceFeedback: Re-check: does this show a part being compared to the whole group?
This compares trucks to cars, which is a part-to-part ratio. For part-to-whole you need 10 + 6 as the second number.
The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
hints: The word 'total' means this is part-to-whole — compare trucks to ALL vehicles, not to cars.
First find the total number of vehicles by adding cars and trucks. The trucks' number goes first.
Add 10 + 6 to find the total vehicles. Then write 6 (the trucks) first and that total second.
onLevel.stemEs: Un estacionamiento tiene 10 autos y 6 camionetas. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a todo de camionetas al total de vehículos?
onLevel.explanationEs: Total de vehículos = 10 + 6 = 16. La razón de camionetas al total es 6:16.
hintsEs: La palabra 'total' significa que esto es parte a todo: compara los camiones con TODOS los vehículos, no con los carros.
Primero halla el número total de vehículos sumando carros y camiones. El número de camiones va primero.
Suma 10 + 6 para hallar el total de vehículos. Luego escribe 6 (los camiones) primero y ese total después.

onLevel.title: Spot the Mistake — Part-to-Whole Ratio

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A class has 9 boys and 6 girls. Write the part-to-whole ratio of girls to the whole class.
workedExample.workEs: Una clase tiene 9 niños y 6 niñas. Escribe la razón parte-a-todo de niñas a toda la clase.

workedExample.label: Write the ratio
workedExample.work: A student writes girls to the whole class as 6:9.
workedExample.workEs: Un estudiante escribe niñas a toda la clase como 6:9.

workedExample.label: Answer
workedExample.work: The part-to-whole ratio of girls to the whole class is 6:9.
workedExample.workEs: La razón parte-a-todo de niñas a toda la clase es 6:9.

onLevel.correctWork: Part-to-whole compares the part to the WHOLE (15), not to the other part. There are 6 girls and 15 students total, so the correct ratio is 6:15.
hints: Look at Step 3. A part-to-whole ratio should use the total from Step 2.
The student used 9 (just the boys) instead of the whole. The whole is 15, so girls to the whole class is 6:15.
onLevel.titleEs: Detecta el error: razón parte a todo
onLevel.explanation: The whole is counted correctly: 9 + 6 = 15 students. The mistake is in the ratio itself — it compares the 6 girls to the 9 boys instead of to the whole class. A part-to-whole ratio has to use the total, so girls to the whole class is 6:15.
onLevel.explanationEs: El total está bien contado: 9 + 6 = 15 estudiantes. El error está en la razón misma: compara las 6 niñas con los 9 niños en vez de compararlas con toda la clase. Una razón parte a todo tiene que usar el total, así que niñas a toda la clase es 6:15.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Parte-a-todo compara la parte con el TODO (15), no con la otra parte. Hay 6 niñas y 15 estudiantes en total, así que la razón correcta es 6:15.
hintsEs: Mira el Paso 3. Una razón parte-a-todo debe usar el total del Paso 2.
El estudiante usó 9 (solo los niños) en vez del entero. El entero es 15, así que niñas a toda la clase es 6:15.

onLevel.title: Find Aliya's Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A trail mix has 6 almonds, 4 raisins, and 2 cashews. Write the ratio of raisins to total pieces.
workedExample.workEs: Una mezcla de frutos secos tiene 6 almendras, 4 pasas y 2 anacardos. Escribe la razón de pasas al total de piezas.

workedExample.label: Answer
workedExample.work: The ratio of raisins to total is 4:8.
workedExample.workEs: La razón de pasas al total es 4:8.

onLevel.correctWork: The total is 12, not 8. The correct ratio is 4:12.
hints: Look at Step 3. Does 8 match the total Aliya found in Step 2?
The total is 12 pieces, so the part-to-whole ratio should use 12, not 8.
onLevel.explanation: Aliya counted the total correctly: 6 + 4 + 2 = 12 pieces. But the ratio she wrote uses 8, which is not the total — it is only the almonds and raisins together. Comparing the 4 raisins to the whole 12 pieces gives 4:12.
onLevel.explanationEs: Aliya contó bien el total: 6 + 4 + 2 = 12 piezas. Pero la razón que escribió usa 8, que no es el total: son solo las almendras y las pasas juntas. Comparar las 4 pasas con las 12 piezas completas da 4:12.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El total es 12, no 8. La razón correcta es 4:12.
hintsEs: Mira el Paso 3. ¿8 coincide con el total que halló Aliya en el Paso 2?
El total son 12 piezas, así que la razón parte-a-todo debe usar 12, no 8.

extending.instructions: Sort each statement — is it a part-to-part ratio or a part-to-whole ratio?

items.text: 3 boys to 5 girls in cooking class
items.textEs: 3 niños a 5 niñas en la clase de cocina
2 tazas de azúcar a 3 tazas de harina

items.text: 4 vegetarian dishes out of 10 total dishes
items.textEs: 4 platos vegetarianos de 10 platos en total

items.text: 3 sweet items out of 10 total items

hints: Look for the words 'out of' or 'total' — those signal a comparison to the WHOLE group.
Ask each card: are BOTH numbers pieces of the group (part-to-part), or is the second number the whole group (part-to-whole)?
Try '3 boys to 5 girls': boys and girls are each just one part of the class — no total is named. Which pile does that point to?
extending.explanation: A part-to-part ratio compares one piece of a group to another piece: 3 boys to 5 girls, 2 cups sugar to 3 cups flour, and 7 savory items to 3 sweet items. A part-to-whole ratio compares one piece to the entire group, and the phrase 'out of ... total' gives it away: 5 girls out of 8 students, 4 vegetarian dishes out of 10, and 3 sweet items out of 10.
extending.explanationEs: Una razón parte a parte compara una porción del grupo con otra porción: 3 niños a 5 niñas, 2 tazas de azúcar a 3 tazas de harina, y 7 platillos salados a 3 dulces. Una razón parte a todo compara una porción con el grupo completo, y la frase 'out of ... total' lo delata: 5 niñas de 8 estudiantes, 4 platillos vegetarianos de 10 y 3 postres de 10.
extending.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada afirmación: ¿es una razón parte a parte o una razón parte a todo?
hintsEs: Busca las palabras 'de un total de' o 'total': esas señalan una comparación con TODO el grupo.
Pregúntale a cada tarjeta: ¿son AMBOS números partes del grupo (parte a parte), o el segundo número es el grupo entero (parte a todo)?
Prueba '3 niños a 5 niñas': niños y niñas son cada uno solo una parte de la clase; no se nombra un total. ¿A qué montón apunta eso?

extending.instructions: Complete the table by writing each ratio in all three forms.
hints: Look at the finished row: '4 cats to 7 dogs' becomes 4 to 7, then 4:7, then 4/7 — same numbers, three costumes.
Keep the numbers and their order the same in every column; only the symbols change (the word 'to', a colon, a fraction bar).
Start with row 2: which number comes first, the 9 red or the 15 total? Keep that order and just change the symbol in each column.
extending.explanation: The same ratio can wear three costumes without changing value: word form uses 'to', colon form uses a colon, and fraction form uses a fraction bar. The numbers and their order stay identical across the row, so '9 red out of 15 total' becomes 9 to 15, 9:15, and 9/15, and '5 wins to 3 losses' becomes 5 to 3, 5:3, and 5/3.
extending.explanationEs: La misma razón puede vestirse de tres formas sin cambiar de valor: en palabras se usa 'to', en la forma de dos puntos se usan los dos puntos, y en la forma de fracción se usa la barra de fracción. Los números y su orden se mantienen iguales en toda la fila, así que '9 red out of 15 total' se escribe 9 to 15, 9:15 y 9/15, y '5 wins to 3 losses' se escribe 5 to 3, 5:3 y 5/3.
extending.instructionsEs: Completa la tabla escribiendo cada razón en las tres formas.
hintsEs: Mira la fila terminada: '4 gatos a 7 perros' se vuelve 4 a 7, luego 4:7, luego 4/7 — los mismos números con tres disfraces.
Conserva los números y su orden en cada columna; solo cambian los símbolos (la palabra 'a', dos puntos, una barra de fracción).
Empieza con la fila 2: ¿qué número va primero, los 9 rojos o el total de 15? Conserva ese orden y solo cambia el símbolo en cada columna.

extending.stem: A bag of marbles has 8 red, 6 blue, and 4 green marbles. Write three different ratios using these quantities: one part-to-part ratio, one part-to-whole ratio, and explain the difference.
extending.sampleAnswer: Part-to-part: red to blue = 8:6. Part-to-whole: green to total = 4:18. The difference is that part-to-part compares two individual groups, while part-to-whole compares one group to the entire collection (8 + 6 + 4 = 18).
extending.hint: Remember to explain which type each ratio is.
hints: You need THREE things: a part-to-part ratio, a part-to-whole ratio, and an explanation of how they differ.
Part-to-part compares two colors. Part-to-whole compares one color to ALL marbles — so you'll need the total first.
Start by finding the whole: add 8 + 6 + 4. Then pick any two colors for your part-to-part ratio, like red to blue.
extending.stemEs: Una bolsa de canicas tiene 8 canicas rojas, 6 azules y 4 verdes. Escribe tres razones distintas usando estas cantidades: una razón parte a parte, una razón parte a todo, y explica la diferencia.
extending.explanation: A part-to-part ratio compares two groups to each other, such as red to blue, 8:6. A part-to-whole ratio compares one group to the total of 8 + 6 + 4 = 18 marbles, such as green to all marbles, 4:18. The difference is what the second number stands for: another part, or the entire set.
extending.explanationEs: Una razón parte a parte compara dos grupos entre sí, por ejemplo rojas a azules, 8:6. Una razón parte a todo compara un grupo con el total de 8 + 6 + 4 = 18 canicas, por ejemplo verdes a todas las canicas, 4:18. La diferencia está en lo que representa el segundo número: otra parte o el conjunto completo.
hintsEs: Necesitas TRES cosas: una razón parte a parte, una razón parte a todo y una explicación de en qué se diferencian.
Parte a parte compara dos colores. Parte a todo compara un color con TODAS las canicas, así que necesitarás el total primero.
Empieza hallando el todo: suma 8 + 6 + 4. Luego escoge dos colores cualesquiera para tu razón parte a parte, como rojo a azul.

extending.stem: Prep Bowl A: Chef Reyes stirs 7 cups of flour with 4 cups of water to make dough. What is the part-to-part ratio of flour to water?
extending.explanation: Part-to-part compares the two ingredients in the order named. Flour to water = 7 to 4, written 7:4.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
11 is the total number of cups, not an ingredient. Part-to-part compares the two ingredients themselves.
extending.stemEs: Tazón de preparación A: el chef Reyes mezcla 7 tazas de harina con 4 tazas de agua para hacer masa. ¿Cuál es la razón parte a parte de harina a agua?
extending.explanationEs: Parte a parte compara los dos ingredientes en el orden en que se nombran. Harina a agua = 7 a 4, escrito 7:4.
hints: A ratio compares two amounts in the exact order the question names them.
Part-to-part compares one ingredient directly to the other ingredient, so there is no total to add here.
The question names flour first, so 7 goes in the first spot — now decide which amount belongs after the colon.
hintsEs: Una razón compara dos cantidades en el mismo orden en que las nombra la pregunta.
Parte a parte compara un ingrediente directamente con el otro, así que aquí no hay que sumar ningún total.
La pregunta nombra primero la harina, así que el 7 va en el primer lugar; ahora decide qué cantidad va después de los dos puntos.

extending.stem: A class has 5 chefs and 7 helpers (12 total). What is the part-to-whole ratio of chefs to the whole class?
extending.explanation: The whole class is 5 + 7 = 12 students. Part-to-whole compares one part to the total, so chefs to whole class is 5:12.
choiceFeedback: Re-check: does this show a part being compared to the whole group?
This is a correct part-to-whole ratio, but for the helpers. Check which group the question asks you to compare to the whole class.
The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
extending.stemEs: Una clase tiene 5 chefs y 7 ayudantes (12 en total). ¿Cuál es la razón parte a todo de chefs a la clase completa?
extending.explanationEs: La clase completa son 5 + 7 = 12 estudiantes. Parte a todo compara una parte con el total, así que chefs a la clase completa es 5:12.
hints: A part-to-whole ratio compares one group to the total group, not to the other part.
Find the whole first by adding the two groups together.
The whole class is 5 + 7 = 12 students. Now decide which number the question names first and put it in front of the colon.
hintsEs: Una razón parte a todo compara un grupo con el grupo total, no con la otra parte.
Primero halla el total sumando los dos grupos.
La clase completa son 5 + 7 = 12 estudiantes. Ahora decide qué número nombra primero la pregunta y colócalo antes de los dos puntos.

extending.stem: “For every” language: Chef Reyes says, “My glaze uses 9 spoons of honey for every 4 spoons of lemon.” Written in colon notation, the ratio of honey to lemon is:
extending.explanation: “For every 9 honey to 4 lemon” is a part-to-part comparison. In colon notation, honey to lemon is 9:4.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
13 is the total number of spoons, so this compares the whole mixture to the lemon. “For every” language compares the two ingredients themselves.
extending.stemEs: Lenguaje de «por cada»: el chef Reyes dice: «Mi glaseado usa 9 cucharadas de miel por cada 4 cucharadas de limón». En notación con dos puntos, la razón de miel a limón es:
extending.explanationEs: «Por cada 9 de miel a 4 de limón» es una comparación parte a parte. En notación con dos puntos, miel a limón es 9:4.
hints: “For every” is ratio language — it compares one amount directly to another amount.
Colon notation writes the quantity named first, then a colon, then the quantity named second.
The sentence names honey first with 9 spoons, so 9 goes before the colon — now decide which number belongs after it.
hintsEs: «Por cada» es lenguaje de razón: compara una cantidad directamente con otra cantidad.
La notación con dos puntos escribe primero la cantidad que se nombra primero, luego los dos puntos y después la segunda cantidad.
La oración nombra primero la miel con 9 cucharadas, así que el 9 va antes de los dos puntos; ahora decide qué número va después.

workedExample.workEs: La razón de pimientos al total de ingredientes es 2:6.

extending.correctWork: Part-to-whole compares the part to the WHOLE (12), not to one other part. The peppers are 2 and the whole is 12, so the correct ratio is 2:12.
hints: Look at Step 3. A part-to-whole ratio should use the total from Step 2.
Chef Mateo used 6 (just the olives) instead of the whole. The whole is 12, so peppers to total is 2:12.
extending.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: la razón de ingredientes de la pizza del chef Mateo
extending.explanation: Chef Mateo counted the whole correctly: 6 + 2 + 4 = 12 toppings. The error is in the ratio — he compared the 2 peppers to the 6 olives instead of to the whole pizza. A part-to-whole ratio uses the total, so peppers to total toppings is 2:12.
extending.explanationEs: El chef Mateo contó bien el total: 6 + 2 + 4 = 12 ingredientes. El error está en la razón: comparó los 2 pimientos con las 6 aceitunas en vez de compararlos con la pizza completa. Una razón parte a todo usa el total, así que pimientos a ingredientes totales es 2:12.
extending.correctWorkEs: Parte-a-todo compara la parte con el TODO (12), no con otra parte. Los pimientos son 2 y el todo es 12, así que la razón correcta es 2:12.
hintsEs: Mira el Paso 3. Una razón parte-a-todo debe usar el total del Paso 2.
El chef Mateo usó 6 (solo las aceitunas) en vez del entero. El entero es 12, así que pimientos a total es 2:12.

extending.stem: A recipe uses 4 cups of milk and 1 cup of cream. What is the ratio of milk to cream?
extending.explanation: A ratio compares quantities in the order given. Milk to cream = 4 to 1, or 4:1.
choiceFeedback: The order matters — what is named first should be first in the ratio.
You added the numbers together — a ratio compares two amounts, not their sum.
5 is the total number of cups, not the amount of cream. This compares the whole recipe to one part instead of milk to cream.
hints: Re-read the question: it asks for milk to cream, in that exact order.
In a ratio, the amount named first goes first. Find the milk amount and the cream amount before you write anything.
Underline the two amounts: milk = 4 cups, cream = 1 cup. Write them in the same order the question names them.
extending.stemEs: Una receta usa 4 tazas de leche y 1 taza de crema. ¿Cuál es la razón de leche a crema?
extending.explanationEs: Una razón compara cantidades en el orden que se indica. Leche a crema = 4 a 1, o 4:1.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta: pide leche a crema, exactamente en ese orden.
En una razón, la cantidad que se nombra primero va primero. Halla la cantidad de leche y la de crema antes de escribir nada.
Subraya las dos cantidades: leche = 4 tazas, crema = 1 taza. Escríbelas en el mismo orden en que las nombra la pregunta.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Understand Ratios is writing the ratio in the wrong order: when asked for the ratio of apple juice to sparkling water in a recipe that uses 3 cups of apple juice for every 2 cups of sparkling water, some students write 2:3 (sparkling water to apple juice) because they list the ingredients in whatever order comes to mind rather than the order the question asks for. The two ratios describe different drinks — 3:2 means 3 cups of juice for every 2 cups of water, while 2:3 would mean only 2 cups of juice for every 3 cups of water. Always match the order of your ratio to the order named in the question: "apple juice to sparkling water" means the apple juice number comes first, giving 3:2.

diagram.title: Main-to-Side Dish Ratio
diagram.caption: Each group keeps the 3:2 ratio; five groups reach 10 side dishes, so the cafeteria needs 15 main dishes.

connect.scenario: The school cafeteria is planning a new lunch menu. They want to offer 3 main dishes for every 2 side dishes. If they have 10 side dishes, the cafeteria manager needs to figure out how many main dishes to prepare.
connect.prompt: For every ___ main dishes the cafeteria serves ___ side dishes, so with 10 side dishes they need ___ main dishes.

check.stem: Keeping the 3:2 ratio, how many main dishes go with 10 side dishes?
check.explanation: 10 sides ÷ 2 = a scale factor of 5. Multiply the mains by that same 5: 3 × 5 = 15 main dishes.

check.stem: What kind of ratio is 3 mains to 2 sides?
choices: Part-to-part, because it compares two separate groups
Part-to-whole, because it compares mains to all dishes
A rate, because it uses different units
check.explanation: Mains and sides are two separate parts, so 3:2 is part-to-part. Part-to-whole would be 3 mains to 5 total dishes.

check.stem: With 15 mains and 10 sides, what is the ratio of mains to TOTAL dishes?
check.explanation: 15 + 10 = 25 total dishes, and 15:25 simplifies to 3:5. That is a part-to-whole ratio.

connect.modelAnswer: The ratio 3 mains : 2 sides stays the same no matter how much food the cafeteria makes. With 10 side dishes the scale factor is 10 ÷ 2 = 5, so they need 3 × 5 = 15 main dishes. That gives 15:10, which simplifies right back to 3:2.

exitTicket.stem: Explain your thinking — A bag of trail mix contains 8 peanuts and 5 raisins. What is the ratio of raisins to total pieces?
exitTicket.explanation: Total pieces = 8 + 5 = 13. The ratio of raisins to total is 5:13.
choiceFeedback: That's peanuts to raisins — the question asks raisins to TOTAL.
That compares raisins to peanuts, not raisins to the whole bag.
You reversed it — put raisins first, then the total.
hints: Careful — this asks for raisins compared to ALL the pieces in the bag, not to the peanuts.
Find the total first by adding peanuts and raisins, then write the raisins' number before the total.
Add 8 + 5 to get the total pieces. Start the ratio with 5 (the raisins), then put that total after the colon.
exitTicket.stemEs: Explica tu razonamiento — Una bolsa de mezcla de frutos secos tiene 8 cacahuates y 5 pasas. ¿Cuál es la razón de pasas al total de piezas?
exitTicket.explanationEs: Total de piezas = 8 + 5 = 13. La razón de pasas al total es 5:13.
choiceFeedbackEs: Eso es cacahuates a pasas — la pregunta pide pasas al total.
Eso compara las pasas con los cacahuates, no las pasas con toda la bolsa.
Lo invertiste — pon las pasas primero y luego el total.
hintsEs: Con cuidado — esto pide las pasas comparadas con todas las piezas de la bolsa, no con los cacahuates.
Halla primero el total sumando los cacahuates y las pasas, y luego escribe el número de las pasas antes del total.
Suma 8 + 5 para obtener el total de piezas. Empieza la razón con 5 (las pasas) y luego pon ese total después de los dos puntos.
